perspective:
Vincent’s available information, in chronological form:

- He is a mechanic and knows Patrick as a long-time friend and construction worker; they met as teenagers and often collaborate using Vincent’s mechanical skills and Patrick’s construction expertise.
- At a local diner, Vincent asks Patrick about a new construction venture. Patrick confirms he is considering it, sees it as a good opportunity to expand his business, thinks it is worth the risk, and says he is still weighing options. Vincent has heard it is risky; he worries about financial security and suggests reconsidering or delaying until more information is gathered. Patrick thanks him and says he’ll think it over.
- Over the next few days, Vincent notices Patrick avoiding detailed discussions about the investment. At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent says he feels Patrick is not telling him everything. Patrick says it is complicated and he did not want to worry Vincent with details. Vincent says he feels betrayed by the lack of transparency and insists they discuss it. Patrick apologizes, says he should have been more open, and proposes sitting down to explain everything.
- During a detailed discussion at Vincent’s garage, Vincent learns Patrick’s investment troubles are serious. Patrick tells him it has been tough and he might lose a significant amount if it does not turn around soon. Vincent offers to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanks him and expresses gratitude for the support.
- A month later at a coffee shop, Vincent says the venture might actually turn a profit. Patrick says it is starting to look up and that he is relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologizes for doubting him earlier and proposes a joint venture. Patrick agrees and suggests working out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick are optimistic about the joint venture. Vincent says their combined skills can make it a success. Patrick agrees and says he is excited. Vincent proposes starting the business plan and outlining every step carefully. Patrick agrees they should cover all bases and set it up for success.
